subject: general
question: A dealer allows a discount of 25% on marked price but still gains 60%. If the cost price is Rs. 1500, what is the marked price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Gain 60% → SP = 1.6 × CP = 1.6 × 1500 = 2400

⇒ 25% discount → SP = 75% of MP

⇒ MP = SP ÷ 0.75 = 2400 ÷ 0.75

⇒ MP = 3200

**∴ Answer = ₹3200**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price = 1500

Gain = 60%

Discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (1 + Gain%)

SP = MP × (1 − Discount%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 1500 × (1 + 60/100)

⇒ SP = 1500 × 1.6 = 2400

⇒ SP = MP × (1 − 25/100)

⇒ 2400 = MP × 75/100

⇒ MP = 2400 × 100 ÷ 75

⇒ MP = 3200

**∴ Final Answer = ₹3200**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Profit Formula:** SP = CP × (1 + Gain/100)

**Discount Formula:** SP = MP × (1 − Discount/100)

**Combined Concept:** First find SP, then back-calculate MP

**Exam Tip:** Always convert % into multiplier form
